edition.witness_note: Single locked witness in repo; second witness not yet locked.

source_text: Imo, inquis, spero ab illo quod et ipsum faciat ad testimonium diversitatis regnum Dei aeternae et coelestis possessionis. Caeterum, vester Christus pristimum statum Judaeis pollicetur, ex restitutione terrae, et post decursum vitae, apud inferos in sinu Abrahae refrigerium. Deum optimum! si reddit placatus, quod et abstulerat iratus. O Deum tuum qui et caedit et sanat, condit mala et facit pacem! O Deum etiam ad inferos usque misericordem! Sed de sinu Abrahae suo tempore. De restitutione vero Judaeae, quam et ipsi Judaei, ita ut describitur, sperant, locorum et regionum nominibus inducti, quomodo allegorica interpretatio in Christum et in Ecclesiam, et habitum et fructum ejus spiritaliter competat, et longum est persequi, et in alio opere digestum, quod inscribimus, De spe fidelium; et in praesenti vel eo otiosum, quia non de terrena, sed de coelesti promissione sit quaestio. Nam et confitemur in terra nobis regnum repromissum; sed ante coelum, sed alio statu; utpote post resurrectionem in mille annos, in civitate divini operis Hierusalem coelo delata, quam et Apostolus matrem nostram sursum designat, et politeuma nostrum, id est, municipatum in coelis esse pronuntians, alicui utique coelesti civitati eum deputat. Hanc et Ezechiel novit, et apostolus Joannes vidit, et qui apud fidem nostram est, novae prophetiae sermo testatur, ut etiam effigiem civitatis ante repraesentationem ejus conspectu futuram in signum praedicarit. Denique proxime expunctum est orientali expeditione. Constat enim, ethnicis quoque testibus, in Judaea per dies quadraginta matutinis momentis civitatem de coelo pependisse, omni meoniorum habitu evanescente de profectu diei, et alias de proximo nullam. Hanc dicimus excipiendis resurrectione sanctis, et refovendis omnium bonorum utique spiritalium copia in compensationem eorum quae in saeculo vel despeximus, vel amisimus, a Deo prospectam. Siquidem et justum, et Deo dignum, illic quoque exultare famulos ejus, ubi sunt et afflicti in nomine ipsius. Haec ratio regni terreni, post cujus mille annos, intra quam aetatem concluditur sanctorum resurrectio, pro meritis maturius vel tardius resurgentium, tunc et mundi destructione, et judicii conflagratione commissa, demutati in atomo in angelicam substantiam, scilicet per illud incorruptelae superindumentum, transferemur in coeleste regnum, de quo nunc sic ideo retractatur, quasi non praedicato apud Creatorem, ac per hoc, alterius Dei Christum probante, a quo primo et solo sit revelatum.
pass_a_gloss: For, you ask, I hope from Him what also He Himself does for a testimony of the diversity of the kingdom of God of eternal and heavenly possession. Moreover, your Christ first promises to the Jews a former state, from the restitution of the earth, and after the course of life, among the dead in the bosom of Abraham refreshment. God the best! if He returns what He had taken away, having been placated, because He had taken it away, being angry. Oh, your God who both strikes and heals, founds evils and makes peace! Oh, God also merciful even to the underworld! But concerning the bosom of Abraham, in its own time. For indeed, concerning the restitution of Judea, which also the Jews themselves, as it is described, hope for, having been led by names of places and regions, how an allegorical interpretation into Christ and into the Church, and its habit and fruit spiritually competes, and it is long to pursue, and it has been digested in another work, which we entitle, On the Hope of the Faithful; and in the present, or it is idle, because the question is not about an earthly, but about a heavenly promise. For we also confess that the kingdom has been promised to us on earth; but before heaven, but in another state; as it were, after the resurrection in a thousand years, in the city of the divine work Jerusalem, which has been lifted up to heaven, which also the Apostle designates as our mother above, and our community, that is, our municipality in the heavens, pronouncing it to be in a certain heavenly city, he deputes it to. This city also Ezekiel knows, and the Apostle John has seen, and the word of the new prophecy, which is among our faith, testifies, so that it also predicts the image of the city before its representation, as a sign to be seen. Finally, it has been recently confirmed by an eastern expedition. For it is consistent, also with pagan witnesses, that in Judea, for forty days, at morning moments, a city hung from heaven, with every habit of the moon vanishing from the progress of the day, and at other times, none from nearby. We say this city is for receiving the resurrection of the saints, and for renewing all spiritual goods, certainly, in compensation for those things which we have despised or lost in the world, foreseen by God. For it is just, and worthy of God, that there also His servants should rejoice, where they are also afflicted in His name. This is the reason for the earthly kingdom, after which, in a thousand years, the resurrection of the saints is concluded, for the merits of the resurrected, sooner or later, then also, with the destruction of the world, and the conflagration of judgment having been committed, having been changed into an atom, into an angelic substance, certainly, through that superindumentum of incorruptibility, we will be transferred into the heavenly kingdom, about which now it is thus retracted, as if it had not been predicted by the Creator, and through this, it proves Christ to be of another God, from whom alone it has been revealed first and only.

choices.why: technical term for garment of incorruptibility

bible_refs.note: the city of the divine work Jerusalem

pass_b_english: You say you hope that He will Himself act as a testimony to the diversity of God's kingdom — the eternal, heavenly possession. Your Christ, meanwhile, promises the Jews their original state: a restored land, and after life ends, refreshment in Abraham's bosom among the dead. God Most Good — if He gives back what He took away in anger, now that He is placated. Oh, your God who both strikes and heals, creates evil and makes peace! (Isaiah 45:7) Oh, a God merciful even to the underworld! But we will return to Abraham's bosom at the proper time.

As for the restoration of Judea — which the Jews themselves hope for, exactly as described, led on by the names of places and regions — tracing how an allegorical interpretation applies spiritually to Christ and the Church, its character and its fruit, would take too long; it is treated in another work, titled *On the Hope of the Faithful*. Here it would be idle, because the question is not about an earthly promise but a heavenly one. We do confess a kingdom promised to us on earth — but before heaven, and in another state: after the resurrection, for a thousand years, in the city of God's work, Jerusalem, lifted up from heaven. The Apostle calls her our mother above (Galatians 4:26), and declares our citizenship — our municipality — to be in heaven, assigning it to a certain heavenly city. Ezekiel knows this city (Ezekiel 40–48), the apostle John has seen it (Revelation 21:10), and the word of the new prophecy among our faith testifies to it, even predicting the city's image as a sign before it appears.

Finally, it was recently confirmed by an eastern expedition. Pagan witnesses agree: in Judea, for forty days, at morning moments, a city hung from heaven, every appearance of the moon vanishing as the day advanced, and at other times none visible from nearby. We say this city is for receiving the resurrection of the saints, and for renewing every spiritual good in compensation for what we have despised or lost in the world, as foreseen by God. For it is just, and worthy of God, that His servants should rejoice there, where they were also afflicted in His name. This is the rationale for the earthly kingdom: after its thousand years, within which the resurrection of the saints is completed — sooner or later, according to the merits of those rising — then, with the world's destruction and the conflagration of judgment, changed in an instant into angelic substance, clothed with that garment of incorruptibility, we will be transferred into the heavenly kingdom. This kingdom is now discussed as if it had not been predicted by the Creator — and thus Christ is proved to belong to another God, from whom alone it was first and only revealed.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Latin text. Pass A provides a faithful literal gloss, and Pass B provides a fluent rendering that correctly incorporates the required scripture citations (Isaiah 45:7, Galatians 4:26, Ezekiel 40–48, Revelation 21:10) based on the context of the Latin clauses. The translation of 'politeuma' as 'citizenship/municipality' and 'superindumentum' as 'garment/superindumentum' is handled well across both versions.
